This next report provides an update on the first year of operations for the green cart program. And also seeks approval on options to adjust the collection for you can see based on seasonal changes. Throughout the first 12 months of the program. The program has diverted over 20,000 tons of organic waste from the landfill. This resulted in a new

increase in our city wide waste diversion rate from 24.5% to over 33%. A survey was conducted last fall to obtain feedback on the program so that we can continue to improve the service of residents. Concerns are that during the peak organic waste seasons. The green carts are full. And that's the

green cart can have nuisance orders. Well, in the winter months, the carts are often not full enough to put out for pickup on every collection period. Green cart collections are provided by city staff and with city resources. The time a route takes to collect is independent or sorry is dependent on the number of carts that are set out and the volume of material collected. Less carts and less material mean the route can be collected more quickly and at less expense. Based on the feedback for see from residents over the past year for options with regards to collection.

We can see for the green cart program have been developed. The first option is status quo, which is to maintain the bi weekly collection year round. The second option is to adjust the winter collection to every four weeks over four months from December until March. So we essentially monthly. The third option is to adjust summer collection to increase collection frequency from weekly or sorry two weekly from April to November.
And the fourth option is a combination of options two and three, which would be to reduce the winter collection and increase summer collection.

Considering all factors, the administration is recommending option to be approved, which is to reduce the winter collection frequency to once every four weeks from December 1st until March 31st. This changes anticipated to result in savings of $162,000 a year or a 17 cents per cart per month.
If approved, this option could be implemented for the upcoming winter. Due to the savings being relatively small in comparison to the total budget that has been approved already for 2025.
It is recommended that any savings be allocated to the stabilization reserve rather than adjusting the utility rates.
Beyond that, any savings from reduced winter collections will be incorporated as part of the 2026 rates as to be presented as part of the 2026-2027 multiyear business plan and budget deliberations.
